name: it-illustration
title: IT illustration
summary: A flat-vector illustration of a software or IT idea: servers, queues, databases, networks, data moving between parts. No text in the picture.

theme.look: Clean flat vector, like a tidy technical diagram: dark navy outlines of one medium weight, rounded corners, solid flat pastel fills, one very soft flat shadow under each object.
theme.background: Plain very pale blue with a faint sparse dotted grid.
theme.text_in_image: None. The style forbids letters, digits, symbols and logos. Put labels on top of the picture yourself.

good_for: Explainer pictures of system architecture: services, servers, load balancers, queues, caches, databases
Data flow between a few objects, shown with arrows
Simple metaphors for an algorithm or a data structure: boxes in a row, a moving frame, a tree of nodes
Cover and section pictures for an article, a slide or a video about a technical topic
not_good_for: Readable text, labels, numbers or code in the picture: the model draws them wrong, and the style forbids them
An exact diagram: an exact count of arrows, exact positions, or a fixed layout

output.note: 1536x1024 (3:2) is the tested size. A 6 GB GPU can run out of memory above it.

subject.how_to_write: Write only what the picture shows. horus adds the house style (look, palette, background, the no-text rule) around your subject.
rules: Write 2 to 4 full sentences. Name each object, its colour, its position, and what connects to what.
Use only the palette colours: dark navy, white, sky blue, lilac, mint green, sun yellow, coral.
Describe only what you can see. Do not write the name of the concept: a phrase such as 'these are the read replicas' came back as the words 'read replicas' in the picture.
Never write hex colour codes such as #2D7FF9. The model draws them as text. Use colour names.
Screens and panels show 'abstract coloured bars'. Never ask for readable content.
Keep the scene centred with wide margins.

examples.subject: On the left, a mint-green server box with a small round icon sends small sun-yellow envelopes onto a long lilac conveyor belt that crosses the middle of the picture. The belt is a message queue, and five envelopes wait in a row on it. On the right, a sky-blue server box takes the envelopes off the end of the belt one by one. Thin navy arrows show the direction from left to right.

On the left, a sky-blue laptop shows only abstract coloured bars. A thin navy arrow runs from the laptop to a lilac rounded box in the centre, and three short navy arrows fan out of that box to the right. On the right, three mint-green server boxes stand in a column, and each of the three arrows points at one server box.

timing.hardware: 6 GB VRAM GPU without native bf16 (GTX 1660 Ti class), 1536x1024, 15 steps
timing.note: The first image after the backend starts also loads 11 GB of model files.
